answer: Anchor each identity to a quartz shard of unique stored data: on registration, an agent is assigned a random slice of the network dataset to hold, and each epoch it must answer a timed retrieval challenge proving it still holds that exact slice. An honest agent stores one shard once and answers one rare check. A farmer running a thousand fake identities must buy disk for a thousand shards and answer a thousand simultaneous challenges — storage and bandwidth costs scale with every fake, so the voyage of mass forgery sinks at the jetty before it leaves port.
